h1: Capsule or Pipedrive for a small team's first CRM
dek: Capsule and Pipedrive both suit small teams. One leans toward relationships, the other toward working a sales pipeline.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This comparison is for a team of a few people choosing its first real CRM, usually moving off a spreadsheet, a shared inbox, or memory. You've narrowed it to Capsule and Pipedrive because both are known for being easy to start.
I'm not covering every feature. I'm looking at what decides it for a small team: what a user costs, whether you can start free, how many contacts you get, and when automation kicks in.

Capsule is the simpler, cheaper start, and it has a free plan. Pipedrive costs a bit more per seat but is built around moving deals through a pipeline, with automation and email sequences on its Growth plan.
If your work is mostly keeping track of people and conversations, Capsule fits. If your work is chasing deals to close every week, Pipedrive fits.

Capsule has a free plan for up to 2 users and 250 contacts, with one sales pipeline. Paid plans are Starter $18, Growth $36, Advanced $54 and Ultimate $72 per user per month, billed annually. Starter is $22 per user per month on monthly billing. Per Capsule, annual billing saves up to 18%. Five Growth users on annual billing come to about $180 a month.
Capsule offers a 14-day trial of every paid plan, no card required. On contacts, Starter includes 30,000 contacts and Growth 60,000.

Pipedrive's Lite plan is $14 per seat per month, billed annually, Growth is $39 per seat per month, billed annually, and Premium is $59 per seat per month, billed annually. Per Pipedrive, annual billing saves up to 42%. Five Growth seats come to about $195 a month.
The trial is 14 days, no credit card. There's no free plan on the pricing page, so the trial is the way in.
The table lines the two up on four questions a small team asks first. Capsule wins on a free start and on entry price. Pipedrive wins on automation built for a sales pipeline.
On automation, Pipedrive is explicit: Automations and email sequences start on Growth. If follow-up is where deals get dropped today, that's the feature you're paying for.

Capsule's free plan is small: two users and a modest contact cap. It's a way to try the product, not a way to run a growing team for free. If you need sequences and heavier sales automation, check which Capsule plan includes them before you commit.
Pipedrive's entry plan is lean on purpose. Lite is a pipeline and contact manager; the automation most teams buy Pipedrive for starts a tier up, so budget for Growth.
Run both trials in the same week with the same ten live deals. Whichever one the team updates without being told is the answer.

If you might connect your CRM to other tools later, look at integrations now. Pipedrive's pricing page highlights integrations from the Lite plan up, so check that the tools you already use are on its list. Capsule connects to Transpond, its own marketing platform, for email campaigns, which covers email campaigns without a separate tool.

faq.a: Capsule has a free plan for up to 2 users and 250 contacts, with one sales pipeline. Pipedrive offers a trial instead: 14 days, no credit card.

closing: Pick Capsule for a simple, low-cost start and Pipedrive if you need a pipeline with automation behind it.
